f.title: Make the privacy notice standalone, clear and itemised, with the purpose and the means to withdraw consent, exercise rights and complain
f.statement: The notice given by the Data Fiduciary to the Data Principal shall (a) be presented and be understandable independently of any other information; (b) give, in clear and plain language, a fair account of the details needed for specific and informed consent, including at the minimum an itemised description of the personal data and the specified purpose(s), with a specific description of the goods or services to be provided or uses enabled; and (c) give the particular communication link to the Data Fiduciary's website or app, and a description of any other means, by which the Data Principal may withdraw consent (as easily as she gave it), exercise her rights under the Act and complain to the Board.
f.clause: Rule 3 (Notice given by Data Fiduciary to Data Principal)
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 760 of 13 November 2025, bilingual Hindi/English; curated from the English text). Bind Data Fiduciaries such as MAHs, sponsors and PV service providers processing digital personal data of patients and reporters. Rules 3 and 5 to 16 apply eighteen months after publication (rule 1(4)). Where consent is the basis of processing.

f.title: Minimum security safeguards: encryption, obfuscation, masking or tokens, and access control
f.statement: A Data Fiduciary shall protect personal data in its possession or control, including processing by a Data Processor, by reasonable security safeguards which shall include at the minimum (a) appropriate data security measures such as encryption, obfuscation, masking or virtual tokens mapped to the data; and (b) appropriate measures to control access to the computer resources used by the Data Fiduciary or Data Processor.
f.clause: Rule 6(1)(a)-(b) (Reasonable security safeguards)
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 760 of 13 November 2025, bilingual Hindi/English; curated from the English text). Rules 3 and 5 to 16 apply eighteen months after publication (rule 1(4)).

f.statement: The minimum reasonable security safeguards under rule 6(1) also include (c) visibility on access to personal data through appropriate logs, monitoring and review, to detect, investigate and remediate unauthorised access; (d) reasonable measures for continued processing if confidentiality, integrity or availability is compromised, such as data backups; and (e) retention of such logs and personal data for one year, for detection, investigation, remediation and continued processing, unless another law requires otherwise.

f.title: Inform each affected Data Principal of a personal data breach without delay, with description, consequences, mitigation and contact
f.statement: On becoming aware of any personal data breach, the Data Fiduciary shall, to the best of its knowledge, intimate each affected Data Principal concisely, clearly and in plain language and without delay, through her user account or a registered mode of communication, of (a) a description of the breach (nature, extent, timing); (b) the likely consequences relevant to her; (c) mitigation measures implemented or being implemented; (d) safety measures she may take; and (e) business contact information of a person able to respond to her queries.
f.clause: Rule 7(1) (Intimation of personal data breach)
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 760 of 13 November 2025, bilingual Hindi/English; curated from the English text). f.title: Send the Board a detailed breach report within 72 hours of becoming aware
f.statement: Within seventy-two hours of becoming aware of the breach, or a longer period the Board allows on written request, the Data Fiduciary shall intimate the Board of (i) updated and detailed information on the description; (ii) the broad facts on the events, circumstances and reasons leading to the breach; (iii) mitigation measures implemented or proposed; (iv) any findings on the person who caused the breach; (v) remedial measures to prevent recurrence; and (vi) a report on the intimations given to affected Data Principals.
f.clause: Rule 7(2)(b) (Intimation of personal data breach)

f.title: Retain personal data, traffic data and processing logs for at least one year, then erase unless another law requires more
f.statement: In respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor, a Data Fiduciary shall retain the personal data, associated traffic data and other logs of the processing for a minimum of one year from the date of processing, for the purposes in the Seventh Schedule, and then cause them to be erased unless further retention is required by any other law or notified by the Government.
f.clause: Rule 8(3) (Time period for specified purpose to be deemed as no longer being served)
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 760 of 13 November 2025, bilingual Hindi/English; curated from the English text). Bind Data Fiduciaries such as MAHs, sponsors and PV service providers processing digital personal data of patients and reporters. Rules 3 and 5 to 16 apply eighteen months after publication (rule 1(4)).
f.exceptions: Longer retention required by any other law (e.g. PV record retention) or notified by the Government.

f.title: Publish the DPO or contact person details on the website or app and in every rights response
f.statement: Every Data Fiduciary shall prominently publish on its website or app, and mention in every response to a communication for the exercise of a Data Principal's rights, the business contact information of the Data Protection Officer, if applicable, or of a person able to answer on its behalf questions about the processing of her personal data.

f.title: Verify that the person giving consent for a child is an identifiable adult parent before processing the child's data
f.statement: A Data Fiduciary shall adopt appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure that verifiable consent of the parent is obtained before processing any personal data of a child, and shall observe due diligence to check that the individual identifying herself as the parent is an identifiable adult (18 or over), by reference to reliable identity and age details it holds, or details voluntarily provided by the individual or through a virtual token issued by an authorised entity.
f.clause: Rule 10(1) (Verifiable consent for processing of personal data of child)
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 760 of 13 November 2025, bilingual Hindi/English; curated from the English text). f.title: Significant Data Fiduciary: carry out a DPIA and audit every 12 months from notification
f.statement: A Significant Data Fiduciary shall, once in every period of twelve months from the date on which it is notified as such (or included in a notified class), undertake a Data Protection Impact Assessment and an audit to ensure effective observance of the Act and the rules.

f.title: Research, archiving or statistical processing is exempt only if it follows the Second Schedule standards
f.statement: The Act does not apply to processing of personal data necessary for research, archiving or statistical purposes if it is carried on in accordance with the standards in the Second Schedule.

f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 760 of 13 November 2025, bilingual Hindi/English; curated from the English text). Bind Data Fiduciaries such as MAHs, sponsors and PV service providers processing digital personal data of patients and reporters. Rules 3 and 5 to 16 apply eighteen months after publication (rule 1(4)). Research, archiving or statistical processing.
f.exceptions: Only if processing follows the Second Schedule standards.

rows.actor: Data Fiduciary carrying out research or statistical processing (e.g. sponsor, epidemiology team)
rows.quote:
16. Exemption from Act for research, archiving or statistical purposes. —The provisions of the Act
shall not apply to the processing of personal data necessary for research, archiving or statistical purposes if
it is carried on in accordance with the standards specified in Second Schedule.
rows.location: Rule 16 (Exemption from Act for research, archiving or statistical purposes)
rows.review_note: Review: exemption, level Permitted. Act s. 17(2)(b) adds that the data must not be used for decisions specific to a Data Principal. Double-check: statement matches the quote.

f.title: Second Schedule standards for research processing: lawful, purpose-limited, minimised, accurate, retained only as needed, secure
f.statement: For processing under the research, archiving or statistical exemption, the Data Fiduciary shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure, in accordance with applicable law, that (a) processing is lawful; (b) it is done for the specified purposes; (c) it is limited to the personal data necessary; (d) reasonable efforts are made for completeness, accuracy and consistency; (e) data is retained only as long as required or as another law requires; and (f) reasonable security safeguards prevent personal data breach, including at Data Processors. The person who determines the purpose and means of processing is accountable for observing these standards.
f.clause: Second Schedule (Standards for processing, see rules 5(1) and 16)
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 760 of 13 November 2025, bilingual Hindi/English; curated from the English text). Bind Data Fiduciaries such as MAHs, sponsors and PV service providers processing digital personal data of patients and reporters. Rules 3 and 5 to 16 apply eighteen months after publication (rule 1(4)). Processing that relies on the research, archiving or statistical exemption (Act s. 17(2)(b), rule 16).
f.processes: Epidemiology / safety studies; Data integrity & records

rows.actor: Data Fiduciary carrying out research or statistical processing (e.g. sponsor, epidemiology team)
rows.location: Second Schedule (Standards for processing, see rules 5(1) and 16)
rows.review_note: Review: standards that condition the research exemption; level Mandatory for anyone relying on it. Double-check: the Schedule is a list of standards without a modal verb; items (e)-(h) are after a page header and outside the quote; held below 90.

f.title: Furnish information to the Central Government when called for, within the period given
f.statement: When the Central Government, through the authorised person in the Seventh Schedule and for the purposes listed there, requires a Data Fiduciary to furnish information, the Data Fiduciary must furnish it within the period specified in the request.
f.clause: Rule 23(1) (Calling for information from Data Fiduciary or intermediary)
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 760 of 13 November 2025, bilingual Hindi/English; curated from the English text). Bind Data Fiduciaries such as MAHs, sponsors and PV service providers processing digital personal data of patients and reporters. Rules 3 and 5 to 16 apply eighteen months after publication (rule 1(4)). Only when the Central Government calls for information.

rows.actor: Data Fiduciary from whom information is called for
rows.deadline: Within the period specified in the request
rows.quote:
23. Calling for information from Data Fiduciary or intermediary. — (1) The Central Government may,
for such purposes of the Act as are specified in Seventh Schedule, acting through the corresponding
authorised person specified in the said Schedule, require any Data Fiduciary or intermediary to furnish such
information as may be called for, within the specified period as may be given in such.
rows.location: Rule 23(1) (Calling for information from Data Fiduciary or intermediary)
rows.review_note: Review: authority power over companies, recorded as a conditional company duty (only when information is called for). Double-check: duty inferred from "require"; held below 90.

f.title: Do not disclose a Government information request to the Data Principal when told not to
f.statement: Where furnishing the information is likely to prejudice the sovereignty and integrity of India or the security of the State, the Central Government may require the Data Fiduciary not to disclose the furnishing to the affected Data Principal or any other person, except with the previous written permission of the authorised person.
f.clause: Rule 23(2) (Calling for information from Data Fiduciary or intermediary)
f.applicability: India; Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E), Gazette of India Extraordinary No. 760 of 13 November 2025, bilingual Hindi/English; curated from the English text). Bind Data Fiduciaries such as MAHs, sponsors and PV service providers processing digital personal data of patients and reporters. Rules 3 and 5 to 16 apply eighteen months after publication (rule 1(4)). Only when the Central Government so requires.

rows.actor: Data Fiduciary from whom information is called for
rows.quote:
(2) Where the disclosure of furnishing of information as referred to in sub-rule (1) is likely to prejudicially
affect the sovereignty and integrity of India or security of the State, the Central Government may require
the Data Fiduciary or intermediary to not disclose such furnishing to affected Data Principal or any other
person except with the previous permission, in writing, of the authorised person.
rows.location: Rule 23(2) (Calling for information from Data Fiduciary or intermediary)
